title: I secured the private route.
subtitle: Five years treated. About ten months without continuity.
source: Case: C01, C06, C10 • First-person account
alt: MJB personal update. After approximately five years of ADHD treatment and ten months without continuity, ADHD Direct confirmed the private Amfexa prescription was sent on 12 October 2026. No completed NHS prescribing handover is evidenced in this review. Delivery, dispensing and recovery remain unconfirmed.

title: Deaths: keep the scope visible.
subtitle: Two different official reporting series.
closing: Do not add them. Neither is an avoidable-death count.
alt: 183 deaths of people subject to Mental Health Act detention were reported to coroners in England and Wales in calendar 2025. Separately, CQC received 314 death notifications in England in financial year 2024/25, comprising 253 detained patients and 61 people subject to community treatment orders. The totals are not additive and neither establishes preventability.

title: An investigation needs an outcome.
subtitle: England and Wales • Calendar 2025 • ALL CAUSES
closing: These are not NHS or mental-health-only totals.
alt: Ministry of Justice data show 35,989 inquests opened and 654 Prevention of Future Deaths reports issued in England and Wales in 2025, across all causes. MJB asks who verifies resulting safety changes. Neither total measures mental-health-only events or proved NHS negligence.

title: CWPT: mixed ratings.
subtitle: Different assessment levels must stay distinct.
closing: A rating is not a completed handover.
alt: CQC rated CWPT trust-level Well-led as Good, published 26 August 2026. Adult community mental-health Safe and Responsive were Requires improvement, published 15 July 2026. Positive findings and concerns coexist. These are service and leadership assessments, not an adjudication of Matthew’s ADHD prescribing decision.

title: Reviews are not interchangeable.
subtitle: Three examples of different accountability processes.
closing: Identify the process. Verify the change.
alt: Three distinct processes: the Lampard statutory inquiry into Essex mental-health inpatient deaths in 2000–2023; the Nottinghamshire CQC special review published March 2024; and the Greater Manchester independent assurance review published May 2026. These examples are not a national count of trusts currently under statutory investigation.

title: The letters kept arriving.
subtitle: The prescribing handover did not.
closing: 305 calendar days: discharge date to dispatch date.
source: Case originals [C01, C03, C06, C10, C11]
alt: Timeline: recorded discharge 11 December 2025, with context disputed; bridge refusal 5 March; cardiology condition and communication controls 28 May; ICB assurance and no single senior case owner on 19 August; privately funded appointment 23 September; private prescription dispatch 12 October. The discharge-to-dispatch date difference is 305 days.

title: The patient had to coordinate.
subtitle: The workload was part of the crisis.
closing: This should not be a condition of getting care.
alt: The mailbox audit found 4,356 retained sent-folder message records from 1 January to 12 October 2026 across two accounts: 2,368 personal and 1,988 advocacy. This includes wider correspondence and is not a care-only or unique-recipient count. Matthew describes coordinating evidence, complaints, referrals and private treatment while disabled by pain and impaired executive function.

title: Close the loop.
subtitle: MJB proposed continuity safeguards
closing: Measure patient outcomes, not just referrals.
alt: MJB proposes six continuity safeguards: named decision-maker, accepted receiving service, interim plan, consideration of treatment and delay risks, review and escalation date, and an accessible written decision. NICE NG87 recommendation 1.5.1 supports continuity of care. The safeguards are proposals, not a statutory entitlement to a particular prescription.
